# Gradient stop order controls

Original OOXML fixture generated by `tools/gradient_stop_order_fixture.py` using
our original shape-theme package. No corpus artwork or third-party fonts are included.
The reference application opened the exact source read-only and exported
`native.pdf`. Source and PDF hashes are recorded in `reference.json`.

Ten rectangles cover all six permutations of three distinct stops, duplicate
interior stops in ordered and unordered lists, reversed tie order, and duplicate
endpoints. The reference application sorts by position stably. At repeated positive positions its
visible band uses the first color; at zero it uses the last color. Canvas's
hard-transition behavior differs. The source XML remains untouched.

`tools/gradient_stop_order_reference.py` evaluates the reference application's native PDF axial
shading functions at 100 positions. This avoids PDFium's raster shading sampling
error (up to six RGB levels in the already-sorted control). The browser compares
these colors within three RGB levels and checks edit/export/reopen, unrelated
package parts, original XML stop order, and exact undo.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.8.36 and 20.1.8.37 define stop positions and their
list; they do not require ascending XML order or specify duplicate-position
resolution. The latter is recorded measured reference behavior, not a proven
contradiction of a normative requirement.
